nodes.name: WO3 nanoseeds electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The FTO substrates were first cleaned by serial ultrasonic washing in acetone, ethanol, 1.0M KOH, and deionized water for 20 min each and dried with a stream of high purity N2. Then the WO3 nanoseeds were deposited onto the FTO substrates by double-potential pulses at -0.40V and 0.20V (versus SCE) for 300s and 15s, respectively, in the solution prepared by dissolving 2g of W powder, 10mL of 30% H2O2 in 30mL of isopropanol and 100mL of deionized water.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of the WO3 NFs Film: ... The WO3 nanoseeds were deposited onto the FTO substrates by double-potential pulses at -0.40V and 0.20V (versus SCE) for 300s and 15s, respectively...

nodes.procedure: The WO3-nanooseed-coated FTO was cleaned and annealed in air at 450°C for 30 min.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal WO3 NFs growth
nodes.procedure: The resulting FTO/WO3 nanoseeds were used as substrates to grow the WO3 nanoflakes film via a hydrothermal synthesis at 180°C for 2h in the precursor solution of 3.0mL 0.05M H2WO4, 0.5mL 6M HCl, 20mg urea, 20mg oxalic acid, and 12.5mL acetonitrile. During the hydrothermal synthesis, the WO3-nanooseed-coated FTO was leaned against the polytetrafluoroethylene reactor and fully immersed in the precursor solution with the side coated with WO3 nanoseeds facing down.
nodes.source_text: The resulting FTO/WO3 nanoseeds were used as substrates to grow the WO3 nanoflakes film via a hydrothermal synthesis at 180°C for 2h...

nodes.name: WO3 NFs final annealing
nodes.procedure: After hydrothermal growth, the obtained WO3 films were rinsed with ethanol and water, and then annealed at 500°C for 1h in air.
nodes.source_text: After hydrothermal growth, the obtained WO3 films were rinsed with ethanol and water, and then annealed at 500°C for 1h in air.

nodes.name: Electrochromic treatment
nodes.procedure: The e-WO3 NFs were prepared in 0.5M LiClO4 solution of propylene carbonate (PC) using a two electrode cell with the r-WO3 as cathode and platinum (Pt) foil as anode. The electrochromic voltage and time were adjusted by a DC Stabilized Power Supply.

nodes.characterization_summary: r-WO3 NFs form crosswise network film with average nanoflake thickness ca. 30 nm and total thickness ca. 900 nm; no noticeable morphological changes after electrochromic treatment at -1.5 V and -3.5 V for 60 s.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The top-view and cross-section-view SEM images of the obtained r-WO3 NFs are shown in Figure 1b,c, respectively, which indicate that the r-WO3 NFs grew crosswise to each other and vertically to the FTO substrate, forming a NFs network film with a total thickness of ca. 900 nm ... No noticeable changes can be observed in the WO3 NFs before and after electrochromism.

nodes.characterization_summary: r-WO3 NFs exhibit monoclinic structure with peaks at 23.12°, 23.59°, 24.38°, and 34.15° corresponding to (002), (020), (200), and (202) planes; electrochromism transforms m-WO3 → t-LixWO3 → c-LixWO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the untreated r-WO3 NFs, the diffraction peaks situated at 23.12°, 23.59°, 24.38°, and 34.15° match well with the (002), (020), (200) and (202) crystal planes of monoclinic WO3, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: UV-vis spectra show band edge absorption at ca. 450 nm for all WO3 samples; electrochromism increases absorption intensity >450 nm but bandgap remains ca. 2.75 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2c, the electrochromic treatment greatly influences the UV–vis spectra especially in the wavelength region longer than 450 nm ... All the WO3 samples, regardless of being electrochromically treated or not, display a bandgap energy of ca. 2.75 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows W⁶⁺ peaks at 35.2 and 37.3 eV, W⁵⁺ at 34.6 and 36.7 eV; O 1s peaks at 529.9 eV (lattice O), 531.6 eV (O_vacancy), 532.4 eV (adsorbed H2O); W⁵⁺ and oxygen vacancy percentages increase with electrochromic time.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The W 4f spectra is composed of two pairs of peaks, corresponding to the 4f7/2 and 4f5/2 peaks of W⁶⁺ located at 35.2 and 37.3 eV and those of W⁵⁺ located at 34.6 and 36.7 eV, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows much stronger resonance signal for e-WO3 than r-WO3, confirming increased oxygen vacancies after electrochromism.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 6c shows that e-WO3 displays a much stronger resonance than r-WO3, which provides solid evidence that electrochromism produces oxygen vacancies in WO3.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mott-Schottky plots show flat band potential φ_fb = 0.950 V vs RHE for r-WO3 and 1.165 V vs RHE for e-WO3; donor density N_D increases from 1.85×10¹⁹ cm⁻³ (r-WO3) to 6.44×10¹⁹ cm⁻³ (e-WO3 at 60 s) and 1.18×10²⁰ cm⁻³ (320 s).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The φ_fb value of r-WO3 is 0.950 V versus RHE, and after electrochromism φ_fb of e-WO3 increases sharply to 1.143 V versus RHE within the first 60 s of coloration and then reaches a saturated value of ca. 1.165 V versus RHE ... the e-WO3 with a coloring time of 60 s has a N_D value of 6.44 × 10¹⁹ cm⁻³, which is nearly 3.5-fold that of r-WO3 (1.85 × 10¹⁹ cm⁻³).

nodes.characterization_summary: Conductivity increases from 6.07×10⁻² S m⁻¹ (r-WO3) to 9.45×10⁻² S m⁻¹ (e-WO3 colored at -1.5 V for 60 s).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The e-WO3 colored at -1.5 V for 60 s possesses a conductivity of 9.45×10⁻² S m⁻¹, which is much larger than the 6.07×10⁻² S m⁻¹ of r-WO3.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows e-WO3 exhibits much smaller charge transfer resistance than r-WO3 at WO3/electrolyte interface under illumination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S13 (Supporting Information) demonstrates that illumination initiates the charge transfer reaction of water oxidation across the WO3/electrolyte interface, and the e-WO3 exhibits a much smaller charge transfer resistance than the r-WO3.
